newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold shrugs off IMF sale decision delay.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold shrugs off IMF sale decision delay.

text.p: Far East gold prices shrugged off any fallout from a delay by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in deciding to sell off some of its gold to help the world's poor, Hong Kong traders said on Tuesday.
A decision was unlikely to be made on Wednesday, when IMF board members resume talks on the controversial proposal after reaching no conclusion last Friday, they said.
But the lack of a decision and the uncertainty it engendered had the market on hold, traders said.
"People buy on rumour and sell on fact, but no one wants to sell aggressively," said one gold trader in Hong Kong.
Gold closed barely firmer on Tuesday after a day of languid and directionless trade, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$383.10/60 an ounce against New York's US$383.00/40 close on Monday.
Local gold ended HK$6 higher at HK$3,531 a tael.
"The IMF delay has kept gold from recovering," a local trader said.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society remained unchanged at -6 on Tuesday.

IMF management, backed by the United States, Britain and most other member nations, has proposed selling five million of the fund's 104 million ounces of gold if needed to help finance stepped-up assistance to poor countries.
But a few nations -- Germany, Italy and Switzerland -- have opposed the proposal, arguing in part that the IMF should not sell gold except in cases of extreme financial emergency.
The IMF board was struggling to garner enough votes in favour of a decision to sell the gold, said one Hong Kong trading sources.
"There's a lot of arm twisting going on behind the scenes and I don't think it will come through," another source said.

If the board is unable to reach an agreement, finance ministers and central bankers of the IMF's policy-setting Interim Committee may have to take up the issue when the meet in Washington on September 29.
